coupling_convention: dimensionless epsilon (U(1)_{B-L} coupling normalized to electromagnetic coupling e); NOT converted to g_BL (would need factor e~0.303). Values are sqrt of the plotted epsilon^2.
notes: PPTA 14.2-yr search for ultralight dark photon dark matter (U(1)_B and U(1)_{B-L}). Paper reports 95% upper limits on epsilon^2 vs dark photon mass (10^-23.5 to 10^-21 eV, i.e. ~2.4e-9 to 2.4e-7 Hz) in Fig.1. Two coupling scenarios presented: U(1)_B and U(1)_{B-L}; I selected VectorBL for the B-L case per guidance, but the paper equally presents a U(1)_B (gauged baryon number) limit. Coupling epsilon is normalized to e (dimensionless), plotted as epsilon^2 (axis 1e-52 to 1e-42). No numerical table of the exclusion curve is given; data_points are digitized/estimated from Fig.1 (uncorrelated B-L curve) and carry large uncertainty. MICROSCOPE WEP comparison gives epsilon<10^-24.07 (B-L) and epsilon<10^-23.28 (B) as horizontal lines. rho0=0.4 GeV/cm^3 assumed.
